A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Nova, with matching methods, benchmarks, and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison after accounting for section moves and model-name refinements.

before.justification: V5 reports original decompilation and binary-similarity experiments, component ablations, embedding visualizations, and attention analyses.

after.justification: V6 retains those original empirical results and adds separate contrastive-loss ablations in Appendix A.4, Table 11.

M1.justification: The three-level hierarchical attention, functionality and optimization contrastive objectives, and downstream fine-tuning procedures remain intact. Added embedding explanations document implementation rather than establish a changed method. The 1B/6B to 1.3B/6.7B labels refine existing model names.

E1.justification: Both use AnghaBench and The-Stack, HumanEval-Decompile, BinaryCorp-3M, and the same six binary-similarity test projects. The new ablations retain HumanEval-Decompile. ARM generalization and alternative assembly collection are discussed without new evaluations.

E2.justification: V6 Table 11 adds two internal comparison variants: Nova without functionality CL and hierarchical attention, and Nova without optimization CL and hierarchical attention. External baseline membership is unchanged; the LongCoder comparison and more precise model-size labels correspond to existing comparisons.

E3.justification: V5 Section 3.2 specifies three-shot prompting for GPT models; v6 Section 4.2 specifies it for every baseline except LLM4Decompile and Nova, and explicitly assigns 20 sampled decompilations to every model. This revises the reported evaluation specification without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.4 separates the contributions of functionality CL and optimization CL while disabling hierarchical attention. V5 ablates contrastive learning jointly. Existing attention-head ablations, similarity ablations, case studies, and embedding and attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds training-seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing. The added ablation rows follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V6 Table 11 newly reports average Pass@1/Pass@10 of 17.05/29.85 with optimization CL alone and 20.40/32.87 with functionality CL alone, both without hierarchical attention. Retained benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged; these are additional results, not improved scores for the full model.

T1.justification: The printed BCSD loss corrects the positive-candidate embedding reference from the undefined f_j^q in v5 Section 2.5 to f_i^p in v6 Section 3.5. Beyond this limited formula correction, the mathematical constraints, objectives, and assumptions remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The conclusion replaces v5's 146.54% decompilation-improvement statement with 14.84–21.58 absolute percentage points in Pass@1/Pass@10, matching the retained abstract and Table 2 differences. V6 also adds a corpus-size summary. The central methodological contributions and two-task effectiveness claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V6 interprets the new ablation as showing greater benefit from functionality alignment than optimization ordering. Appendix A.1 newly explains why linked executable-derived assembly better matches practical analysis than gcc -S output, while leaving alternative collection experiments to future work. Existing limitations are relocated rather than removed.

D1.justification: V6 newly specifies source-token embedding pooling, batchwise contrastive-loss computation, and CodeArt-based BCSD evaluation with embedding normalization, distinguishing it from unnormalized training. Model-access pointers now list nova-1.3b and nova-6.7b instead of nova-6.7b and nova-6.7b-bcr. Existing hardware and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds six references, including Asm2Vec, Debin, DIRE, graph-based binary similarity, and neural-network reverse engineering. It also removes the blanket characterization that earlier task-specific models are built from scratch. Nova's principal positioning relative to existing assembly models remains intact.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, and limitations move to Appendix A.9. Local rewrites clarify data collection, embeddings, evaluation, and the conclusion. Model names, acknowledgments, publication headers, and bibliography formatting are revised, while most exposition is retained.

P2.justification: V6 adds Table 11 for the separate-loss ablations and renumbers the subsequent appendix tables. Table headings and model labels are refined, Figure 4 subcaptions change, and existing figures and tables undergo resizing or relocation. The retained visual analyses are not replaced.

improvement.justification: The separate-loss ablation strengthens evidence about the individual objectives, and added embedding and evaluation details improve reproducibility. The conclusion also aligns its performance summary with Table 2. These are limited gains: benchmark evidence remains largely unchanged, and the new claim of approximately 4.3 million assembly functions appears to include Table 1's C functions, introducing a small counting inconsistency.
